fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on ship-steps-rebase-clean): The new rebase step runs plain rhiza ship rebase, which runs the local gate (make gate, up to an hour) on the merged head before the push (internal/api/ship_rebase.go header). But the leaf's statement and acceptance, and the decision ship-steps-rebase-clean-merge, give it no stall. With no stall, a command step gets the watchdog's DefaultCommandLimit of 30m (internal/api/watchdog_policy.go:26, StallLimit at :151), so the daemon's watchdog would stop and retry the rebase partway through the gate. ship-change-classic.toml:60-71 notes exactly this and sets stall = "70m" on every step that runs ship rebase or ship gate (rebase, rebase-merge, gate-rebase-merge and others); the builtin's gate step also sets stall = "70m". The acceptance should require stall = "70m" (at least the gate's) on the rebase step, and its failure case should fail when it is missing. The critic confirmed it: Checked: internal/api/ship_rebase.go's header says ship rebase runs the project's local gate on the merged head before pushing while CI is unstable. watchdog_policy.go:26 sets DefaultCommandLimit to 30m, and StallLimit (:151) uses it for a command step that has no stall. ship-change-classic.toml:60-71 says every step that runs the gate needs a stall above the gate's hour, and sets stall = "70m" on each one; the builtin's own gate step (ship-change.toml:50) does the same. The leaf's statement and acceptance give the new rebase step no stall, so the watchdog can stop and retry it partway through the gate. That is a real defect the acceptance would let through, so major stands. How should it be settled?
